summary:
Observed in review of FS.GG.SDD `upgrade` owner-skill replacement (FS-GG/FS.GG.SDD#1155, merged as #1158); the blocking defect was found by the independent reviewer, not by the author's tests.

**The defect.** The provenance write was batched with the skill writes and did not depend on them. A read-only `references` directory partway through a skill let some writes fail while the provenance still recorded the new pack's digests and version for files that were never written. The next `upgrade` then compared a record that lied against the disk and failed permanently with exit 2, which also blocked the re-seed of every other skill. A write refused by the write-edge digest re-check produced the same wrong record.

**The rule.** Emit the provenance write only after every file write and removal of the step has been interpreted; claim only what landed; record a replaced skill all-or-nothing (rows, dropped rows, package version, manifest digest) so one failed file leaves the whole skill's record as it was. Make the next run able to finish: a file already at the PACK's digest counts as unedited, and a desired file whose record is stale is a target even when the disk already matches, so a partial or killed run, including one whose files were all written but never recorded, completes on re-run. Name the CLI as the workspace's last writer only when every file landed, otherwise a partial run bars its own completion.

**Evidence.** The reviewer killed the process at seven points and every one healed; the tests cover a read-only directory mid-skill, a killed run, a fully written but unrecorded skill, and a refused write.

**Scope.** Owner-sourced skills (drivers and owner product skills) in `upgrade`; legacy scaffold provenance only.
title: A provenance record is a claim about files: write it after the files, and record only what landed
